notes: Sources: docs/dem_governing_equations_background_20261011.md (§5.3; §10.3 literature counts; §11 limits); CLAUDE.md MPM sections (2026-06-07 … 06-17). In one 7:3 bed, global viscous damping carries 58 % of the plate reaction during compression — an open issue (damping share 57.9 % measured on one 7:3 bed during compression; ledger DEMP-01, open). Selected literature survey (22 studies; author classification, not a systematic review): softened SE modulus 0/22; yield or hardness cap 7/22; linear hysteretic law 1/22; global damping in dry compaction none. Young's modulus reference: our DFT E_VRH = 22.06 GPa (literature DEM input 22.1 GPa, Bazzoun 2026 [8]); the bulk modulus K / B0 = 26.23 GPa is a separate quantity; the glass-electrolyte value 24 GPa (Sakuda 2013 [15]) is a different material system. The DEM statement is about this implementation (fixed spherical shapes, hooke/hysteresis), not about DEM in general. MPM parameters: 2D E = 1.53 GPa, σy = 0.15 GPa; 3D E = 1.53 GPa, ν = 0.49, σy = 0.30 GPa (next slide). Presenter figure (right, blank): MPM 3D render of the DEM-scaffold bed (AM fixed, SE material points), e.g. python3 scripts/viz_mpm_morphology.py --se <SE material points .npy> --scaffold <AM scaffold .csv> --y 0.5 --out morphology.png (actual files required; MPM renders are not tracked in the repository). Do not present the MPM image as an independent validation of the DEM bed.

Reproduced from So et al., J. Power Sources 508, 230344 (2021), Fig. 4a
notes: Sources: CLAUDE.md "3D MPM compaction — 3-fix calibration" (K = E/(3(1−2ν)) = 25.5 GPa vs DFT B0 26.23); our DFT E_VRH 22.06 GPa; Bazzoun 2026 [8] uses E_SE = 22.1 GPa for Li6PS5Cl; the sulfide-glass value 24 GPa (75Li2S·25P2S5, Sakuda 2013 [15]) is a different material system and is not used on the slide. σy = 0.30 GPa was selected in the pure-SE calibration sweep (0.15 → 5.6 %, 0.20 → 6.7 %, 0.25 → 9.0 %, 0.30 → 10.0 %), inside the literature range. Claims ledger CL-94: the pure-SE 10 % value is a calibration target (lab standard sample, unpublished); it is not a literature anchor — our earlier literature attribution was withdrawn. Shear-only softening (ν = 0.49) keeps K = 25.5 GPa close to the DFT reference B0 = 26.23 GPa; softening the bulk modulus over-crushed the bed. "Tested alternatives" = DPC volumetric cap and real-E runs (docs/mpm_dpc_cap_crosscheck.md); the statement is limited to the tested models. Scaffold calculations (AM skeleton from the DEM bed) — status: Earlier: cell-filled SE, bidirectional servo — historical, not a DEM-seeded validation. Current registered runs: DEM-seeded SE, stress-controlled servo — f = 0 completed; f(a) execution failed. AM-load-sharing hypothesis: verdict pending. The current statuses refer to the registered servo runs (--protocol servo; primary endpoint = final thickness after servo convergence). AM load sharing remains a candidate explanation for over-compaction; the final hypothesis verdict is pending. The earlier thickness agreement is not shown: it comes from a different initialization and loading protocol and cannot serve as the validation value of the DEM-seeded runs (SEM-02). Literature crop: So et al. 2021 calibrate a contact-plasticity parameter on the relative density vs pressure of a sulfide SE (their Fig. 4a, experimental points from Sakuda et al.) — a literature example of calibrating an effective contact parameter on pure-SE compaction data.

Faces are joined by a harmonic mean with
upper bound only within the same geometry, properties and boundaries
VGCF as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-line insulator, polymer as spheres; a registered 104-arm study keeps the σ(e⁻)
figure: presenter — 3D current-flow views, contact network and voxel (left) · this work, 104-arm study (right)
σ(e⁻) vs VGCF wt%: campaign means (96 primary arms), three voxel sizes;
notes: Sources: CLAUDE.md "σ 를 내는 솔버는 둘이다" table and CL-81. Finite-volume conservation on the phase grid gives electrical (σ, φ) and thermal (κ, T) transport on the same structure. The voxel solver has no interface-resistance term by default (the film mechanism exists but is off): this makes it an ideal-interface model and an upper bound only for the same geometry, phase properties and boundary conditions — not a physical upper bound; geometric necks still cost resistance inside the voxel grid. The 4.04× (contact-free / full network, n = 157) is a ratio inside the contact-network model. Additives: carbon fibres (VGCF) as diameter-preserving segments, PTFE as a centre-line insulator, a conductive polymer as true-diameter spheres. Pre-registered 104-arm study: the electronic-conductivity order across 1–4 wt% VGCF holds across the tested voxel sizes and grid-origin offsets (72/72) — docs/data/phase_a_rep100_20260930/README.md (104 arms, 72/72 adjacent-composition comparisons with no threshold violation; order only is the registered estimand; increments are technical report only; replay difference 0.00000 %); docs/report_20261021 G6 (voxel σe means; contact resistance not included; figure F_vgcf redrawn from G6). Stamp conventions: CLAUDE.md SR-01 (sphere stamp, centerline PTFE = CL-60). Presenter figures (left, blank): (i) contact-network current pathways of the 7:3 bed — scripts/network_current.py dump <7:3 result folder> → webapp DEM 3D viewer "current flow" (same bed, same H0/FULL ionic solution, 1 V, colour = j = |I|/A; "top 50 % of current" = edges carrying the top half of the current share, not the top half by count); (ii) STEP3 phase grid and the 1 V current-density field of the same voxel solution (A cm⁻²; state origin, voxel size, phase mapping, electrode rule, run hash).

This work (left) · figure: presenter — bed view, layered start and after eight revolutions (right)
M = 1: fully mixed; error bars = within-run SD; all ten runs reach M ≈ 0.96–1.00, so this bin grid cannot separate the arms;

notes: Sources: docs/reviews/mixer_layered_prereg_20260921.md §2 (verdict line), §5 (report wording), §6 (readout 2026-09-30); docs/data/mixer_final10_20260930/ (ten runs; figure F_mix1 redrawn from the registered final values, report_20261021 G7). Registered estimand: paired contrast of the final Lacey index between the arm without NCM–NCM cohesion and the reference-cohesion arm, three seeds, 16×16×4 bins: Δ = +0.0012, seed-to-seed SE 0.0073 ⇒ |Δ| ≤ SE ⇒ registered "no segregation" category ("direction and size not resolved" — in this model, this drum, the tested inputs and this bin convention; not "no effect", not "equivalent"). Coarser grids (report only): 12×12×3 Δ −0.0156, SE 0.0058 (ambiguous); 8×8×2 Δ +0.0081, SE 0.0144. Negative control (no cohesion): M ≥ 0.8 in all three grids; floor check 10/10; flatness 30/30; QC 30/30. The two cohesion matrices differ in NCM–NCM and NCM–wall adhesion together; the comparison is not a reproduction of real coating or of powder flowability. Contract qualifier (Codex wording, 2026-09-28): the result is a comparison of mixing indices after eight revolutions in the specified soft-contact model; in the reference state the maximum stored-frame overlap was 4.7–5.8 % particle–particle and 4.5–5.7 % at the wall, so the registered 1 % condition was not met; the effect of the overlap error on the mixing index has not been verified. Conditions: three phases, 100,000 particles, drum radius 13.1 mm, 75 rpm. Presenter figure (right, blank): bed view of one run, layered start and after eight revolutions (webapp bed view; display only).

notes: Sources: docs/data/mixer_highbo_devrot_prelim_20261002/README.md, mixer_highbo_devbo_prelim_20261003/README.md, mixer_highbo_devu_prelim_20261006/README.md (development data; one seed; two revolutions; no pass/fail line; not used for any verdict; not mixed with the confirmatory seeds). ΔM = M(arm without NCM–NCM cohesion) − M(arm), bins 16×16×4 · 12×12×3 · 8×8×2: reference cohesion +0.010 / −0.006 / +0.008; NCM–NCM cohesion ×10 +0.83 / +0.93 / +0.99; ×30 +1.88 / +2.43 / +3.16; all pairs ×10 +0.24 / +0.17 / +0.10; all pairs ×14 +0.87 (16×16×4 failed the volume-coverage check) / +0.48 / +0.27. The 16×16×4 cells of the ×10 and ×30 NCM runs also failed that check. Negative M values of the strongly cohesive arms lie outside the Lacey range [0, 1] (their start-state variance is smaller); ΔM therefore mixes a start-state difference with the post-rotation difference. The ×10 / ×30 levels were chosen after seeing the first exploratory contrast (post-hoc); NCM–NCM and NCM–wall adhesion change together (joint intervention); the uniform runs scale all nine cohesion matrix elements and include SE stiffening. No sentence about "real coating effect" or "real powder" is made. Presenter figure (right, blank): bed snapshots of the arm without NCM–NCM cohesion vs a cohesive arm after two revolutions (webapp bed view).

notes: Sources: docs/hetero_thesis.md (ratified 2026-10-05) §2-1 · §2-2 · §2-8: W_ij ≈ 2√(γ_i γ_j); ΔW = W_AA + W_SS − 2 W_AS = 2(√γ_A − √γ_S)² ≥ 0; pair Bond number ∝ W·R*/(ρ g R³) of the smaller particle — at equal surface energy the SE–SE pair Bond number is about 194× that of the large-NCM pair and SE→NCM adhesion is 1.8× SE–SE (arithmetic estimates); for SE–SE clusters to survive in an uncoated bed the ratio γ_NCM/γ_SE would have to be below about 0.31 — that ratio is not known (open decision). Predictions P1–P3 of the thesis: uncoated beds keep SE–SE clustering above random; coating removes it; the mixing difference carries into the compacted SE pathway. The present cohesion model does not yet contain that mechanism (NCM–NCM cohesion was varied, not SE–SE). Left figure: docs/data/mixer_highbo_devu_prelim_20261006/README.md §3 — fraction of SE in SE–SE clusters (bin 1, after two revolutions): 0.401 [0.143, 0.542] without NCM–NCM cohesion; 0.954 [0.875, 0.957] all pairs ×10; 0.988 [0.981, 0.988] all pairs ×14 (ranges = dump-resolution [certain, possible]; difference only where ranges do not overlap; one seed; development data). Confirmatory 18-run block: registered, on hold after the Codex rounds (docs/reviews/mixer_highbo_prereg_20260927.md); no "real coating effect" sentence.
